sections.h2: Where is Breckinridge County and what is it like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Breckinridge County lies on the Ohio River in western Kentucky, across from Perry County, Indiana, and is the largest of the four counties compared here by area. It covers 586 square miles, of which 567 are land. Hardinsburg is both the county seat and the largest city, and Cloverport and Irvington are the other incorporated cities. Grayson, Ohio and Hancock counties border it, and Meade and Hardin counties lie to the east.

The county was cut from Hardin County in 1799 and was the 38th Kentucky county formed. Cloverport shipped coal oil from the Victoria mines in the nineteenth century, and Rough River Dam State Resort Park was developed on the southern edge in the 1950s. Voters ended 105 years of local prohibition in a January 29, 2013 election, so Breckinridge is now a wet county.

Breckinridge keeps Central time, while the neighboring Meade and Hardin county areas to the east are on Eastern time. A seller coordinating a closing across the county line should confirm the time zone of every office involved.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Breckinridge County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 21,503 residents for July 2025, up 5.2 percent from the 2020 count of 20,432. That makes it the fastest-growing of the four counties compared here, ahead of Bullitt at 5.1 percent. At 35.9 people per square mile, though, it is the sparsest.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $156,700 (2020 to 2024).
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 81.4 percent, with 8,069 households.
  • Median gross rent: $733 a month.
  • Median household income: $55,843, with 18.3 percent of residents below the poverty line.
  • Building permits in 2025: 14, against 10,952 housing units in July 2025.

At the 2020 count, about a quarter of Breckinridge's 10,704 housing units were vacant, a much higher share than in Bullitt County. Fourteen building permits in 2025 shows how little new construction competes with existing houses.

Work patterns look different from the Louisville-side counties. About 52.6 percent of residents 16 and older are in the civilian labor force, the mean commute is 32.7 minutes, and the county had 283 employer establishments with 2,480 jobs in 2023, a 0.8 percent drop from 2022. Retail sales in 2022 were $217.4 million, or $10,370 per resident. Broadband subscriptions reach 83.9 percent of households, which matters to anyone showing a rural property to buyers who work from home.

sections.h2: Which Breckinridge County office does what?
sections.html:
The sheriff collects, the PVA values, and the county clerk holds unpaid bills. The Sheriff's Office sits at 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, in Hardinsburg, keeps weekday hours from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central, and answers at 270-756-2361. Mail goes to PO Box 127, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. The sheriff collects roughly $11 million a year for the state, county, schools and special districts.

Questions about the homestead exemption or the assessment go to the PVA at 270-756-5154. Delinquent real estate bills from earlier years go to the County Clerk, 270-756-2246, which gives payoff amounts.

sections.h2: What are the Breckinridge County tax payment dates?
sections.html:
The sheriff's notice for the 2026 bills said they would be mailed by October 29, and an owner who has none by November 10 should call for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment open November 1 and run to 4 p.m. Central on April 15. The schedule printed on every bill has these stages, and a postmark counts as proof of timely payment.

Breckinridge County Sheriff's payment stages (source: Breckinridge County Sheriff's Office)
WindowAmount owed
November 1 to 30Face amount less 2%
December 1 to 31Face amount
January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21%
After April 15Pay at the County Clerk's office

Dates and penalty percentages are set by statute and the Kentucky Revenue Cabinet, and the sheriff has no room to negotiate them.

sections.h2: How does paying a Breckinridge County bill work in practice?
sections.html:
The sheriff will take only the exact amount on the bill. A short payment comes back to you, and there are no partial payments. Several bills can go in one payment.

  • Online: a convenience fee of 1.5 percent, with a $1.50 minimum on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on amounts over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck are accepted.
  • By mail or in person: check or money order with the payment voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form must travel with the payment, and online payers who want to opt out must pay by mail or at the office instead.

A cancelled check works as a receipt, and a stamped self-addressed envelope gets you a mailed one.

sections.h2: How are taxes divided when a Breckinridge County house sells?
sections.html:
The bill is issued to the person who owned the property on January 1. If you sold after that date, the bill still arrives in your name, and pass it on to the new owner. The closing agent usually prorates each party's share on the settlement statement.

The sheriff's office will not take a prorated payment from two people, though. One or both parties must pay the full bill. Ask the closing attorney who will carry the payment and whether the buyer will receive a credit for it.

sections.h2: How can a Breckinridge County owner dispute a valuation?
sections.html:
The assessment date is January 1, and the PVA's field visits cover every property in the county about once in four years. If a new value looks wrong, book a conference with the PVA during the weeks the tax roll is open to inspection. The roll opens on the first Monday in May and stays open thirteen days.

Only after the conference may you file with the county clerk, who acts as clerk to the local board of assessment appeals. The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends. Come with photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or sales of similar homes. Boards decide on documents, and an appeal with none is denied.

sections.h2: Is there a senior or disability reduction in Breckinridge County?
sections.html: Homeowners 65 or older, and owners who are totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption on the home they live in. The state set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. The sheriff points all exemption questions to the PVA, and also says that checking your exemption is the first thing to do when a bill feels heavy.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Breckinridge County property tax?
sections.html: After April 15 the bill is taken from the sheriff and entered at the county clerk as delinquent, with a lien on the property. Interest adds 1 percent per month, and clerk and county attorney commissions follow. The county attorney sends notices and the clerk advertises the list before any sale, and a bill that reaches the sale list can be bought by a third party. If you plan to sell a Breckinridge County house with old tax unpaid, order the payoff before the closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

faqs.q: What is the Breckinridge County sheriff's tax office address?
faqs.a: The office is at 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Mail payments go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, starting November 1. Online payments carry a convenience fee, and the full exact amount of the bill must be paid in one transaction.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff accepts only the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

faqs.q: When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?
faqs.a: It starts February 1 and runs to April 15. After that, the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed. At closing, the agent usually prorates the year, and the full bill still has to be paid to the sheriff in one amount.
